mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate signals an expansionary monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, which in turn drives up stock prices and results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when the federal funds rate decreases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 6% triggers a slowdown in consumer spending, leading to decreased demand for goods and services, and ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when the unemployment rate exceeds 6%.

mechanism_narrative: When the housing starts series (HOUST) and the retail sales series (RSAFS) both increase by more than 5% over the past 3 months, it signals a strong consumer demand, leading to increased economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase by > 5% in 3 months
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of the instances when both HOUST and RSAFS increase by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average signals an increase in supply, leading to decreased prices and increased demand, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO exceeds its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) both increase by more than 2% over the past 6 months, it signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, and ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both increase by > 2% in 6 months
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces positive 5-day returns in more than 30% of the instances when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increase by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the payroll employment series (PAYEMS) by more than 1% over the past 3 months signals a slowdown in the labor market, leading to decreased consumer spending and ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when PAYEMS decreases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the GDP series (GDPC1) increases by more than 2% over the past 6 months, it signals a strong economic growth, leading to increased demand for goods and services, and ultimately resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of the instances when GDPC1 increases by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average signals a decrease in supply, leading to increased prices and decreased demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average.
